title: Impersonal 3: Advice (следует, стоит, лучше)
description: A softer modal family for giving advice. Следует is the formal 'ought to.' Стоит says the action is worth doing. Лучше is 'had better.' All three sit in the impersonal slot with a dative person plus an infinitive.
descriptionRussian: Более мягкая модальная семья для советов. «Следует» — формальное «следует». «Стоит» сообщает, что действие имеет смысл. «Лучше» — «лучше бы». Все три стоят в безличной позиции с дательным падежом человека и инфинитивом.
intro: Three ways to give advice, and the difference between them is mostly register rather than meaning. One belongs in writing and formal speech, the other two in ordinary conversation. Choosing the formal one in a casual exchange is not an error, but it lands the way 'one ought to' lands in English.
rules: Frame: (dative person) + следует / стоит / лучше + infinitive, the same impersonal scaffolding as the necessity lesson.
Следует is formal advice ('ought to'). Стоит is value advice ('is worth doing'). Лучше is mild urgency ('had better').
Register: следует in writing and formal speech; стоит and лучше in everyday speech.
The person advised goes in the dative: тебе следует, Маше лучше, ему стоит. Лучше never changes form.
Negation: не следует, не стоит are standard. For 'had better not', put не before the infinitive: тебе лучше не идти.
examples: Тебе следует поговорить с врачом. (You ought to speak with a doctor.) Formal advice; dative person тебе.
Стоит подумать об этом. (It is worth thinking about this.) General recommendation; no dative.
Маше лучше остаться дома сегодня. (Masha had better stay home today.) Mild urgency; dative person Маше.
Тебе стоит позвонить ей сегодня. (You should call her today.) Personal tip; perfective infinitive.
Не стоит так волноваться. (No need to worry like that.) Negated value advice; imperfective infinitive.
Тебе лучше не идти туда одному. (You had better not go there alone.) Negation before the infinitive.

tables.title: The advice family at a glance

items.prompt: Тебе _____ поговорить с врачом, твой кашель не проходит.
items.promptEnglish: You ought to talk to a doctor; your cough is not going away.
items.hint: Formal advice from one person to another. Which word names the 'ought to' reading?
items.explanation: Следует carries the formal 'ought to' reading and fits medical advice. Лучше would soften this to 'had better.' Пора is timing ('it is time'), not advice. Хочется reads as 'I feel like,' the wrong modality.

items.promptEnglish: It is worth thinking about a new job.
items.hint: General value advice without a dative person.
items.explanation: Стоит is the value-advice word ('is worth doing'), exactly the English 'it is worth.' Пора is timing, not value. Нельзя is prohibition, the opposite. Хочется is 'I feel like,' a personal-feeling reading.

items.prompt: Тебе _____ позвонить ей сегодня, она ждёт.
items.promptEnglish: You should call her today; she is waiting.
items.hint: A personal tip with a dative person, value advice.
items.explanation: With the dative person тебе, стоит gives a personal recommendation ('you should'). Нельзя is prohibition. Пора is timing. Должен needs a nominative subject (ты должен), so it cannot pair with the dative тебе.

items.promptEnglish: Masha had better stay home; she has a cold.
items.hint: Mild urgency: 'had better,' not 'ought to' and not 'must.'
items.explanation: Лучше is 'had better' in an impersonal sentence with the dative person Маше. Следует would be 'ought to' (formal). Пора is timing. Должна would need Маша in the nominative ('Маша должна остаться'), a personal-subject sentence, not impersonal.

items.prompt: Не _____ так волноваться, всё будет хорошо.
items.promptEnglish: There is no need to worry like that; everything will be fine.
items.hint: Negated value advice: 'no need to bother.'
items.explanation: Не стоит is the standard 'no need to, do not bother.' Не пора would be timing and is rare. Хочется is personal feeling. Можно is permission, not advice.

items.promptEnglish: In the report one ought to list all the sources.
items.hint: Formal, written register. Which word belongs in a report?
items.explanation: Следует is the formal 'ought to' that fits written and official style, so it suits a report. Хочется is 'I feel like.' Можно is permission. Пора is timing, not a written instruction.

items.promptEnglish: You ought to rest - you work too much.
items.hint: Formal advice: the frozen form + an infinitive.
items.explanation: Следует is impersonal: it never conjugates, and an infinitive follows: тебе следует отдохнуть. Следуешь and следуют wrongly conjugate it; отдыхаешь is a finite verb where the infinitive belongs.

items.prompt: _____ туда идти: там всё равно закрыто.
items.promptEnglish: There's no point going there - it's closed anyway.
items.hint: The negative of value advice: which order?
items.explanation: The negative advice is не стоит + infinitive: не стоит туда идти ('not worth going'). Стоит не reverses the order illegally; нельзя не would be a double negative meaning 'must'.

items.promptEnglish: You'd better not go there alone.
items.hint: The 'had better not' order: which words, in which order?
items.explanation: The warning is лучше + не + infinitive: тебе лучше не идти туда одному. 'Не лучше' would compare ('no better'); нет cannot negate an infinitive.

blanks: Тебе _____ позвонить маме, она волнуется. (You had better call your mom; she is worried.)
Этот фильм очень хороший, его _____ посмотреть. (This film is very good; it is worth watching.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: First blank: 'had better' is mild urgency, which лучше carries. Second blank: 'is worth watching' is value advice, which стоит carries. Нельзя is prohibition and хочется is personal feeling, so neither fits an advice reading.

sentenceBuilding.translation: You ought to talk to a doctor.
sentenceBuilding.hint: Dative person + следует + infinitive. Formal advice.

sentenceBuilding.translation: Masha had better stay home today.
sentenceBuilding.hint: Dative person + лучше + infinitive. Mild urgency.

sentenceBuilding.translation: It is worth thinking about this.
sentenceBuilding.hint: General value advice, no dative person. Start the sentence with стоит.

sentenceBuilding.answer: Тебе лучше не идти туда одному.
sentenceBuilding.translation: You had better not go there alone.
sentenceBuilding.hint: For 'had better not', put не right before the infinitive.

errorCorrection.sentence: Уже поздно, тебе должен идти домой.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: It is late; it is time for you to go home.
errorCorrection.explanation: With a dative person (тебе), the sentence is impersonal: пора ('it is time to'). Должен is a personal-subject word that agrees with a nominative subject (ты должен), so 'тебе должен' mixes the two frames illegally.

errorCorrection.sentence: Этот фильм очень скучный, его стоит смотреть.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: This film is very boring; it is not worth watching.
errorCorrection.explanation: 'Очень скучный' frames negative advice, so не стоит ('not worth it') fits: его не стоит смотреть. The bare стоит would recommend the boring film, the opposite of the context. Нельзя would forbid it outright, which is stronger than advice.

minimalPairs.context: Тебе _____ не идти на работу, ты болен.
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: You had better not go to work; you are ill.
minimalPairs.explanation: With не sitting in front of the infinitive, the frame is лучше: тебе лучше не идти ('you had better not go'). Стоит cannot take не there; it negates in front of itself instead (тебе не стоит идти).

minimalPairs.context: _____ посмотреть этот фильм, он очень хороший.
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: It is worth watching this film; it is very good.
minimalPairs.explanation: Стоит is value advice ('it is worth'), exactly what 'очень хороший' invites. Следует would be a formal 'ought to', too official for a casual film recommendation.

categorySorting.instruction: Sort each sentence by the kind of advice it gives.

items.word: Тебе лучше не идти туда одному.

reviewVocab.definition: ought to / should (formal advice; impersonal word with an optional dative person; preferred in writing and formal speech)
reviewVocab.example: В предложении «Тебе следует поговорить с врачом» слово «следует» выражает формальный совет.

reviewVocab.definition: is worth (doing) (value advice; impersonal word; negation не стоит = 'no need to bother')
reviewVocab.example: В предложении «Стоит подумать об этом» слово «стоит» сообщает, что действие имеет смысл.

reviewVocab.definition: had better (mild urgency; the comparative of хорошо used as a fixed advice word; 'had better not' = лучше не + infinitive)
reviewVocab.example: В предложении «Маше лучше остаться дома» слово «лучше» выражает мягкую настойчивость.
